land.text: 'Asia Minor' (north of the Taurus) that Antiochus Hierax demanded from his brother Seleucus II

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Seleucid Empire shape of 239-226 still holds this land; the Seleucid dossier should show it contested (240-237) and then ceded to Hierax (237-228).

land.text: 'putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains', which Attalus I gained after his victories of c. 230-228

successors.note: Attalus's control was 'tenuous'; Achaeus recovered the Seleucid lands by 221 (Attalus I page, 'within two years' of 223).

capitals.name: Sardis (probable seat, page silent)
capitals.note: No page names a seat. Sardis is the only city the pages tie to his army: Attalus won a battle 'near Sardis in the spring of 228 BC'. Unverified; a gap-filler should check the War of the Brothers page. Longitude corrected from 26.03 to 28.04 (Sardis page: 38.48833 N 28.04028 E; reviewer me-05-x).

rulers.name: Antiochus Hierax
rulers.title: king in Asia Minor
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 240-226 BC'; he lost his possessions in Asia Minor by 228 and 'was killed in Thrace in 226 BC'. Ruler span cut to the state's end (228); he lived as a landless claimant to 226 (reviewer me-05-x).

correction.text: Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus: 'Seleucus left the country beyond the Taurus to his brother'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria draws this land inside the Seleucid Empire for 239-226 (2.06 M km2, 949 cells of Anatolia without the Cilician plain, about 240,000 km2). No infobox area for Hierax. The pages give no boundary: the Seleucid 239 outline within Anatolia, minus Cilicia south of the Taurus, is a reading. 240-238 is the contested claim; the cession follows Ancyra (c. 239 on the Hierax page, c. 237 on the Seleucus II page).

region.text: Asia Minor north of the Taurus, claimed from Seleucus II

ledger.note: 240: Antiochus Hierax sets himself up as king in Asia Minor against Seleucus II. Infobox 'Reign: 240-226 BC'; 'A year later [after 246], probably under the influence of his mother, Antiochus demanded possession of Asia Minor from his brother'. The Seleucus II page: he 'had set himself up as a rival in Asia Minor against Seleucus, supported by their domineering mother Laodice'.

region.text: Asia Minor north of the Taurus, fought over in the War of the Brothers

ledger.note: 240: Seleucus II turns on his brother once peace with Ptolemy is made. 'In 241 BC, Seleucus made peace with Ptolemy III Euergetes and then tried to recover the territories his brother took from him.' The page gives no first campaign; the Lydia fight comes before Ancyra.

region.text: Asia Minor north of the Taurus

ledger.note: 237: Hierax wins at Ancyra. 'the brothers met at the Battle of Ancyra around 237 BC' and 'With the support of Mithridates II of Pontus and the Galatians Antiochus Hierax was victorious'; the Hierax page dates Ancyra 'ca. 239 BC' after 'an initial loss in Lydia'.

region.text: Asia Minor north of the Taurus

ledger.note: 237: Seleucus II gives up Asia Minor. 'Seleucus left the country beyond the Taurus to his brother.' The cession is dated by the battle, not by a treaty.

region.text: the lands between Pergamon and the Seleucid heartland that Pergamon held by 225

ledger.note: 230: Attalus I of Pergamon takes on Hierax and his Galatian allies. 'Attalus defeated the Gauls and Antiochus at the Battle of Aphrodisium', then won three further battles; the page dates the campaign c. 230-228 (the Hierax page gives an attack on Pergamon in c. 238, which the Attalus page puts at 238-235 against the Galatians alone).

228: Attalus's run of victories over Hierax includes the battle 'near Sardis in the spring of 228 BC' (Attalus I page); the last fight it names, the Battle of the Harpasus in Caria, is undated, so the war is closed in 228.

region.text: Asia Minor north of the Taurus, as Hierax held it

ledger.note: 228: Hierax loses Asia Minor to Pergamon. 'Attalus gained putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains' (tenuous); the Hierax page: 'All his possessions taken away, Antiochus still tried to replace his brother in Syria and Mesopotamia'. The pergamon dossier dates the gain c. 227.

region.text: Asia Minor north of the Taurus

ledger.note: 228: Hierax is left without land; he is 'killed in Thrace in 226 BC' (the Seleucus II page: 'killed by robbers in c. 226 BC', after fleeing to Armenia; the Attalus I page has him perhaps in Bithynia). The state ends with the loss of its land, not with his death.

wars.name: War of the Brothers (Seleucid civil war)

zones.text: Asia Minor north of the Taurus

wars.outcome: Hierax won at Ancyra (c. 239 or c. 237) with Mithridates II of Pontus and the Galatians; 'Seleucus left the country beyond the Taurus to his brother'. The Hierax page lists his coalition as 'Cappadocia, Bithynia and a certain number of Galatians'.
wars.note: The Hierax page dates Ancyra ca. 239; the Seleucus II page around 237. The war's start is inferred from the 241 peace with Ptolemy; the Seleucid East was lost in the same years (Parthia c. 238, Bactria 235).

wars.name: Attalus I's war against Antiochus Hierax and the Galatians

zones.text: the lands between Pergamon and Sardis

wars.outcome: Attalus won at Aphrodisium and three more battles, one 'near Sardis in the spring of 228 BC', and gained 'putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains'.
wars.note: Pergamon dates the same war c. 230-227.

certainty.note: Hierax's land is a reading of 'Asia Minor north of the Taurus'; no page gives a frontier.

sources.title: Antiochus Hierax
sources.note: Reign 240-226; demand for Asia Minor; Ancyra ca. 239; coalition; killed in Thrace 226. Names no capital.

sources.title: Seleucus II Callinicus
sources.note: 241 peace, Ancyra around 237, 'Seleucus left the country beyond the Taurus to his brother', Parthia and Bactria lost.

sources.title: Attalus I
sources.note: Aphrodisium and the spring 228 battle near Sardis; 'putative control' of Seleucid Asia Minor; Achaeus 223.

notes: Three pages (budget 2-5). Not opened: the 'War of the Brothers' article (not tried by title; the seleucid-empire dossier says it did not load) and Mithridates II of Pontus; the first battles and the Lydia fight are undated on the pages. Dates differ: Ancyra ca. 239 (Hierax page) against around 237 (Seleucus II page); the Pergamene gain 228 here, c. 227 in kingdom-of-pergamon. The type is rebel (a Seleucid prince holding land against the king for twelve years). The land is a reading: the Cliopatria Seleucid shape of 239 within Anatolia, minus Cilicia. seleucid-empire should show the contest 240-237 and a loss to this state 237-228; kingdom-of-pergamon's contest and gain should name this state as counterpart, not seleucid-empire. Sardis as seat is unverified. The Cappadocia, Bithynia and Pontus allies are in the war entry only: no page dates their own gains.
